title: Prakrama 1, Sarga 4. On the Descents
html:
The Lord's companions as portions of the Lord, of gods and of sages; the story of Haridasa; the two kinds of avatara: the avataras of the ages and the avataras for a particular purpose

Verse 1

अथ श्रुत्वा तु तत्सर्वं श्रीदामोदरपण्डितः।
उवाच परमप्रीतः कथ्यतां नृहरेः कथाम्॥१॥

atha śrutvā tu tatsarvaṁ śrīdāmodarapaṇḍitaḥ|
uvāca paramaprītaḥ kathyatāṁ nṛhareḥ kathām||1||

atha — then; shrutva — having heard; tu — indeed; tat — that; sarvam — all; shri-damodara-panditah — Sri Damodara Pandita; uvacha — said; parama-pritah — greatly pleased; kathyatam — let be told; nrihareh — of Nrihari (the Lord); katham — the story.

1Having heard all this, Sri Damodara Pandita, greatly pleased, said: "Tell us, then, the story of Nrihari1.

Verse 2

के के तत्रावतारेषु स्ववतीर्णा महीतले।
अवताराश्च कतिधा तान्वदस्वानुपूर्वशः॥२॥

ke ke tatrāvatāreṣu svavatīrṇā mahītale|
avatārāśca katidhā tānvadasvānupūrvaśaḥ||2||

ke ke — who and who; tatra — there; avatareshu — in the descents; su-avatirnah — descended; mahi-tale — to the earth; avatarah — the descents; cha — and; katidha — of how many kinds; tan — them; vadasva — tell; anupurvashah — in order.

2Who came down to the earth in these descents? And of how many kinds are the descents? Tell me of them in order."

Verse 3

इति श्रुत्वा द्विजाग्र्यस्य वचनं श्रीमुरारिकः।
उवाच परमप्रीत्या श्रूयतामिति सादरम्॥३॥

iti śrutvā dvijāgryasya vacanaṁ śrīmurārikaḥ|
uvāca paramaprītyā śrūyatāmiti sādaram||3||

iti — thus; shrutva — having heard; dvija-agryasya — of the foremost of the twice-born; vachanam — the words; shri-murarikah — Sri Murari; uvacha — said; parama-pritya — with great affection; shruyatam — listen; iti — thus; sa-adaram — respectfully.

3Hearing these words of the foremost of the twice-born, Sri Murari answered with great affection and respect: "Listen!

Verse 4

अथ ते कथयाम्यन्यत्स्वांशावतरणं हरेः।
शुद्धभक्ततया ख्यातान्भक्तानीश्वररूपिणः॥४॥

atha te kathayāmyanyatsvāṁśāvataraṇaṁ hareḥ|
śuddhabhaktatayā khyātānbhaktānīśvararūpiṇaḥ||4||

atha — now; te — to you; kathayami — I tell; anyat — another thing; sva-amsha-avataranam — the descent of the own portions; hareh — of Hari; shuddha-bhaktataya — as pure devotees; khyatan — renowned; bhaktan — the devotees; ishvara-rupinah — who are forms of the Lord.

4Now I shall tell you of something else — of the descent of Hari's own portions, the devotees who are forms of the Lord, though renowned as pure devotees.

Verse 5

आदौ जातो द्विजश्रेष्ठः श्रीमाधवपुरी प्रभुः।
ईश्वरांशो द्विधा भूत्वाद्वैताचार्यश्च सद्गुणः॥५॥

ādau jāto dvijaśreṣṭhaḥ śrīmādhavapurī prabhuḥ|
īśvarāṁśo dvidhā bhūtvādvaitācāryaśca sadguṇaḥ||5||

adau — first; jatah — was born; dvija-shreshthah — the best of the twice-born; shri-madhava-puri — Sri Madhava Puri; prabhuh — the master; ishvara-amshah — a portion of the Lord; dvidha — twofold; bhutva — having become; advaita-acharyah — Advaita Acharya; cha — and; sad-gunah — of good qualities.

5First was born the best of the twice-born, the master Sri Madhava Puri. A portion of the Lord, dividing in two, appeared both as him and as Advaita Acharya, rich in virtues2.

Verse 6

तयोः शिष्योऽभवद्देवश्चन्द्रांशश्चन्द्रशेखरः।
स आचार्यरत्न इति ख्यातो भुवि महायशाः॥६॥

tayoḥ śiṣyo'bhavaddevaścandrāṁśaścandraśekharaḥ|
sa ācāryaratna iti khyāto bhuvi mahāyaśāḥ||6||

tayoh — of the two; shishyah — the disciple; abhavat — became; devah — the divine; chandra-amshah — a portion of Chandra (the Moon); chandrashekharah — Chandrashekhara; sah — he; acharya-ratnah — Acharyaratna; iti — thus; khyatah — renowned; bhuvi — on earth; maha-yashah — of great fame.

6The disciple of them both was the divine Chandrashekhara, a portion of the Moon; of great fame, he is renowned on earth as Acharyaratna.

Verse 7

श्रीनारदांशजातोऽसौ श्रीमच्छ्रीवासपण्डितः।
गन्धर्वांशोऽभवद्वैद्यः श्रीमुकुन्दः सुगायनः॥७॥

śrīnāradāṁśajāto'sau śrīmacchrīvāsapaṇḍitaḥ|
gandharvāṁśo'bhavadvaidyaḥ śrīmukundaḥ sugāyanaḥ||7||

shri-narada-amsha-jatah — born as a portion of Sri Narada; asau — he; shrimach-chhrivasa-panditah — Sriman Srivasa Pandita; gandharva-amshah — a portion of a Gandharva; abhavat — was; vaidyah — the physician (of the Vaidya caste); shri-mukundah — Sri Mukunda; su-gayanah — the fine singer.

7Sriman Srivasa Pandita was born as a portion of Sri Narada, and Sri Mukunda of the Vaidya (physician) caste, the fine singer, as a portion of a Gandharva.

Verse 8

श्रीमच्छ्रीहरिदासोऽभून्मुनेरंशः शृणुष्व तत्।
कथितं नागदष्टेन ब्राह्मणेन यथा पुरा॥८॥

śrīmacchrīharidāso'bhūnmuneraṁśaḥ śṛṇuṣva tat|
kathitaṁ nāgadaṣṭena brāhmaṇena yathā purā||8||

shrimach-chhri-haridasah — Sriman Sri Haridasa; abhut — was; muneh — of a sage; amshah — a portion; shrinushva — hear; tat — that; kathitam — told; naga-dashtena — by a snake-bitten; brahmanena — brahmana; yatha — as; pura — formerly.

8Sriman Sri Haridasa was a portion of a sage. Hear how this was once told by a brahmana bitten by a snake3.

Verse 9

आदौ मुनिवरः श्रीमान् रामो नाम महातपाः।
द्राविडे वैष्णवक्षेत्रे सोऽवात्सीत्पुत्रवत्सलः॥९॥

ādau munivaraḥ śrīmān rāmo nāma mahātapāḥ|
drāviḍe vaiṣṇavakṣetre so'vātsītputravatsalaḥ||9||

adau — formerly; muni-varah — an excellent sage; shriman — illustrious; ramah — Rama; nama — by name; maha-tapah — of great austerity; dravide — in Dravida; vaishnava-kshetre — in a Vaishnava holy place; sah — he; avatsit — lived; putra-vatsalah — fond of his son.

9Long ago in Dravida, in a Vaishnava holy place, there lived an illustrious sage named Rama, the best of sages, a great ascetic, who loved his son dearly.

Verse 10

तस्य पुत्रेण तुलसीं प्रक्षाल्य भाजने शुभे।
स्थापिता साऽपतद्भूमावप्रक्षाल्य पुनश्च ताम्॥१०॥

tasya putreṇa tulasīṁ prakṣālya bhājane śubhe|
sthāpitā sā'patadbhūmāvaprakṣālya punaśca tām||10||

tasya — his; putrena — by the son; tulasim — the tulasi; prakshalya — having washed; bhajane — in a vessel; shubhe — clean; sthapita — placed; sa — it; apatat — fell; bhumau — on the ground; aprakshalya — without washing; punah — again; cha — and; tam — it.

10His son washed some tulasi and placed it in a clean vessel, but it fell to the ground, and without washing it again

Verse 11

पित्रेऽददात्पुनः सोऽपि श्रीरामाख्यो महामुनिः।
ददौ भगवते तेन जातोऽसौ यवने कुले॥११॥

pitre'dadātpunaḥ so'pi śrīrāmākhyo mahāmuniḥ|
dadau bhagavate tena jāto'sau yavane kule||11||

pitre — to the father; adadat — gave; punah — then; sah api — he too; shri-rama-akhyah — named Sri Rama; maha-munih — the great sage; dadau — offered; bhagavate — to Bhagavan; tena — therefore; jatah — was born; asau — he; yavane — in a Yavana; kule — family.

11he gave it to his father, and the father, the great sage named Sri Rama, offered it to Bhagavan. For that reason he was born in a family of Yavanas (Muslims).

Verse 12

स धर्मात्मा सुधीः शान्तः सर्वज्ञानविचक्षणः।
ब्रह्मांशोऽपि ततः श्रीमान्भक्त एव सुनिश्चितः॥१२॥

sa dharmātmā sudhīḥ śāntaḥ sarvajñānavicakṣaṇaḥ|
brahmāṁśo'pi tataḥ śrīmānbhakta eva suniścitaḥ||12||

sah — he; dharma-atma — righteous; sudhih — wise; shantah — peaceful; sarva-jnana-vichakshanah — versed in all knowledge; brahma-amshah — a portion of Brahma; api — also; tatah — therefore; shriman — illustrious; bhaktah — a devotee; eva — truly; su-nishchitah — without doubt.

12He is righteous, wise, peaceful and versed in all knowledge; moreover, he is a portion of Brahma4, and therefore the illustrious Haridasa is beyond doubt a true devotee.

Verse 13

अवधूतो महातेजा नित्यानन्दो महत्तमः।
बलदेवांशतो जातो महायोगी स्वयं प्रभुः॥१३॥

avadhūto mahātejā nityānando mahattamaḥ|
baladevāṁśato jāto mahāyogī svayaṁ prabhuḥ||13||

avadhutah — the Avadhuta; maha-tejah — of great power; nityanandah — Nityananda; mahattamah — the greatest; baladeva-amshatah — as a portion of Baladeva; jatah — was born; maha-yogi — the great yogi; svayam — himself; prabhuh — the Lord.

13The Avadhuta Nityananda, the greatest of all, of mighty power, was born as a portion of Baladeva5; He is the great yogi, the Lord Himself.

Verse 14

न तस्य कुलशीलानि कर्माणि वक्तुमुत्सहे।
अपि वर्षशतेनापि बृहस्पतिरपि स्वयम्॥१४॥

na tasya kulaśīlāni karmāṇi vaktumutsahe|
api varṣaśatenāpi bṛhaspatirapi svayam||14||

na — not; tasya — his; kula-shilani — family and character; karmani — deeds; vaktum — to describe; utsahe — I venture; api — even; varsha-shatena — in a hundred years; api — even; brihaspatih — Brihaspati; api — even; svayam — himself.

14I do not venture to describe His family, character and deeds: even Brihaspati himself, in a hundred years,

Verse 15

वक्तुं नेशेऽपरे किं वा वयं हि क्षुद्रजन्तवः।
श्रीकृष्णद्वितीयश्चापि गौराङ्गप्राणवल्लभः॥१५॥

vaktuṁ neśe'pare kiṁ vā vayaṁ hi kṣudrajantavaḥ|
śrīkṛṣṇadvitīyaścāpi gaurāṅgaprāṇavallabhaḥ||15||

vaktum — to tell; na ishe — is not able; apare — others; kim va — how much less; vayam — we; hi — indeed; kshudra-jantavah — petty creatures; shri-krishna-dvitiyah — the second (form) of Sri Krishna; cha api — and also; gauranga-prana-vallabhah — dear as life to Gauranga.

15could not tell of them — what then of others, of petty creatures like us! He is the second form of Sri Krishna, dear to Gauranga as life itself.

Verse 16

अन्ये च शतशो जाता देवाश्च मुनिपुङ्गवाः।
पृथिव्यामंशभावेन तान्न संख्यातुमुत्सहे॥१६॥

anye ca śataśo jātā devāśca munipuṅgavāḥ|
pṛthivyāmaṁśabhāvena tānna saṁkhyātumutsahe||16||

anye — others; cha — and; shatashah — by hundreds; jatah — were born; devah — gods; cha — and; muni-pungavah — eminent sages; prithivyam — on earth; amsha-bhavena — as portions; tan — them; na — not; samkhyatum — to enumerate; utsahe — I venture.

16And many others — hundreds of gods and eminent sages — were born on earth as portions; I do not venture to count them.

Verse 17

अथावतारो द्विविधः पुरुषस्य प्रकीर्तितः।
युगावतारः प्रथमः कार्यार्थेऽपरसम्भवः॥१७॥

athāvatāro dvividhaḥ puruṣasya prakīrtitaḥ|
yugāvatāraḥ prathamaḥ kāryārthe'parasambhavaḥ||17||

atha — next; avatarah — the descent; dvi-vidhah — of two kinds; purushasya — of the Purusha (the Supreme Person); prakirtitah — is declared; yuga-avatarah — the avatara of the age; prathamah — the first; karya-arthe — for a (particular) task; apara-sambhavah — the appearance of the other.

17Next: it is declared that the descents of the Purusha are of two kinds. The first is the avatara of the age (yuga-avatara); the other appears for a particular task.

Verse 18

युगावताराः कथ्यन्ते ये भवन्ति युगे युगे।
धर्मं संस्थापयन्ति ये तान् शृणुष्व यथाक्रमम्॥१८॥

yugāvatārāḥ kathyante ye bhavanti yuge yuge|
dharmaṁ saṁsthāpayanti ye tān śṛṇuṣva yathākramam||18||

yuga-avatarah — avataras of the ages; kathyante — are called; ye — those who; bhavanti — appear; yuge yuge — in age after age; dharmam — dharma; samsthapayanti — establish; ye — who; tan — of them; shrinushva — hear; yatha-kramam — in order.

18Those are called avataras of the ages who appear in age after age and establish dharma. Hear of them in order.

Verse 19

सत्ये युगे ध्यान एकः पुरुषस्यार्थसाधकः।
तदर्थेऽवतरच्छुक्लश्चतुर्बाहुर्जटाधरः॥१९॥

satye yuge dhyāna ekaḥ puruṣasyārthasādhakaḥ|
tadarthe'vataracchuklaścaturbāhurjaṭādharaḥ||19||

satye yuge — in the Satya age; dhyanah — meditation; ekah — alone; purushasya — of man; artha-sadhakah — accomplishes the goal; tat-arthe — for that purpose; avatarat — descended; shuklah — the White One; chatur-bahuh — four-armed; jata-dharah — wearing matted locks.

19In the Satya age meditation alone leads a man to the goal. For this purpose the White One descended, four-armed, with matted locks;

Verse 20

सहस्रचन्द्रसदृशः सदा ध्यानरतो मुनिः।
सर्वेषामेव जन्तूनां ध्यानाचार्यो बभूव ह॥२०॥

sahasracandrasadṛśaḥ sadā dhyānarato muniḥ|
sarveṣāmeva jantūnāṁ dhyānācāryo babhūva ha||20||

sahasra-chandra-sadrishah — like a thousand moons; sada — always; dhyana-ratah — absorbed in meditation; munih — a sage; sarvesham eva — of all; jantunam — living beings; dhyana-acharyah — the teacher of meditation; babhuva ha — became.

20like a thousand moons, a sage always absorbed in meditation, He became the teacher of meditation for all living beings.

Verse 21

त्रेतायां यज्ञ एवैको धर्मः सर्वार्थसाधकः।
तत्र यज्ञः स्वयं जातः स्रुक्स्रुवादिसमन्वितः॥२१॥

tretāyāṁ yajña evaiko dharmaḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ|
tatra yajñaḥ svayaṁ jātaḥ sruksruvādisamanvitaḥ||21||

tretayam — in the Treta age; yajnah — sacrifice; eva — alone; ekah — sole; dharmah — dharma; sarva-artha-sadhakah — accomplishing all aims; tatra — then; yajnah — Yajna; svayam — himself; jatah — was born; sruk-sruva-adi-samanvitah — with sacrificial ladles and the rest.

21In the Treta age the one dharma that achieves every aim is sacrifice. Then Yajna Himself was born, with the sacrificial ladles and the other implements.

Verse 22

याज्ञिकैर्ब्राह्मणैः सार्धं यज्ञभुक् स जनार्दनः।
यज्ञमेवाकरोज्जिष्णुर्जनान्सर्वानशिक्षयत्॥२२॥

yājñikairbrāhmaṇaiḥ sārdhaṁ yajñabhuk sa janārdanaḥ|
yajñamevākarojjiṣṇurjanānsarvānaśikṣayat||22||

yajnikaih — with sacrificing; brahmanaih — brahmanas; sardham — together; yajna-bhuk — the enjoyer of sacrifice; sah — he; janardanah — Janardana; yajnam — sacrifice; eva — indeed; akarot — performed; jishnuh — the Victorious; janan — people; sarvan — all; ashikshayat — taught.

22Together with brahmanas who performed sacrifice, He, Janardana, the enjoyer of sacrifice, the Victorious One, Himself performed sacrifice and taught it to all the people.

Verse 23

द्वापरे तु युगे पूजा पुरुषार्थाय कल्प्यते।
इति ज्ञात्वा स्वयं विष्णुः पृथुरूपो बभूव ह॥२३॥

dvāpare tu yuge pūjā puruṣārthāya kalpyate|
iti jñātvā svayaṁ viṣṇuḥ pṛthurūpo babhūva ha||23||

dvapare tu yuge — in the Dvapara age; puja — worship; purusha-arthaya — for the goal of human life; kalpyate — is ordained; iti — thus; jnatva — knowing; svayam — himself; vishnuh — Vishnu; prithu-rupah — in the form of Prithu; babhuva ha — appeared.

23In the Dvapara age worship is ordained for attaining the goal of life. Knowing this, Vishnu Himself appeared in the form of Prithu6.

Verse 24

पूजां चकार धर्मात्मा लोकानां चानुशासनम्।
कारयामास पूजायां सर्वेषामभवन्मनः॥२४॥

pūjāṁ cakāra dharmātmā lokānāṁ cānuśāsanam|
kārayāmāsa pūjāyāṁ sarveṣāmabhavanmanaḥ||24||

pujam — worship; chakara — performed; dharma-atma — the righteous one; lokanam — of the people; cha — and; anushasanam — instruction; karayam asa — carried out; pujayam — to worship; sarvesham — of all; abhavat — turned; manah — the mind.

24Righteous, He Himself performed worship and instructed the people in it, and the minds of all turned to worship.

Verse 25

कलौ तु कीर्तनं श्रेयो धर्मः सर्वोपकारकः।
सर्वशक्तिमयः साक्षात्परमानन्ददायकः॥२५॥

kalau tu kīrtanaṁ śreyo dharmaḥ sarvopakārakaḥ|
sarvaśaktimayaḥ sākṣātparamānandadāyakaḥ||25||

kalau tu — in Kali; kirtanam — kirtana; shreyah — the highest good; dharmah — the dharma; sarva-upakarakah — benefiting all; sarva-shakti-mayah — full of all powers; sakshat — directly; parama-ananda-dayakah — bestowing supreme bliss.

25But in Kali the highest good is kirtana: the dharma that benefits all, full of every power, directly bestowing the highest bliss.

Verse 26

इति निश्चित्य मनसा साधूनां सुखमावहन्।
जातः स्वयं पृथिव्यां तु श्रीचैतन्यो महाप्रभुः॥२६॥

iti niścitya manasā sādhūnāṁ sukhamāvahan|
jātaḥ svayaṁ pṛthivyāṁ tu śrīcaitanyo mahāprabhuḥ||26||

iti — thus; nishchitya — resolving; manasa — in mind; sadhunam — to the saintly; sukham — happiness; avahan — bringing; jatah — was born; svayam — himself; prithivyam — on earth; tu — indeed; shri-chaitanyah — Sri Chaitanya; maha-prabhuh — Mahaprabhu.

26Having resolved thus in His mind, Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu Himself was born on earth, bringing happiness to the saintly7.

Verse 27

कीर्तनं कारयामास स्वयं चक्रे मुदान्वितः।
युगावतारा एते वै कार्यार्थे चापरान् शृणु॥२७॥

kīrtanaṁ kārayāmāsa svayaṁ cakre mudānvitaḥ|
yugāvatārā ete vai kāryārthe cāparān śṛṇu||27||

kirtanam — kirtana; karayam asa — caused to be performed; svayam — himself; chakre — performed; muda-anvitah — full of joy; yuga-avatarah — the avataras of the ages; ete — these; vai — indeed; karya-arthe — for a task; cha — and; aparan — of the others; shrinu — hear.

27Full of joy, He Himself sang kirtana and moved others to sing it. These are the avataras of the ages. Hear now of the others — those who descend for a particular task.

Verse 28

मात्स्ये तु वेदोद्धरणं कौर्मे मन्दारधारणम्।
वाराहे धारणं भूमेर्नारसिंहे विदारणम्॥२८॥

mātsye tu vedoddharaṇaṁ kaurme mandāradhāraṇam|
vārāhe dhāraṇaṁ bhūmernārasiṁhe vidāraṇam||28||

matsye — as the Fish; tu — indeed; veda-uddharanam — the rescue of the Vedas; kaurme — as the Tortoise; mandara-dharanam — the bearing of (Mount) Mandara; varahe — as the Boar; dharanam — the upholding; bhumeh — of the earth; narasimhe — as Narasimha; vidaranam — the tearing apart.

28As the Fish — the rescue of the Vedas; as the Tortoise — the bearing of Mount Mandara; as the Boar — the lifting up of the earth; as Narasimha — the tearing apart (of Hiranyakashipu);

Verse 29

चक्रे दनुजराजस्य वामने भुवनश्रियम्।
जिग्ये तु भार्गवः क्षौणीं जित्वा राज्ञः सुदुर्मदान्॥२९॥

cakre danujarājasya vāmane bhuvanaśriyam|
jigye tu bhārgavaḥ kṣauṇīṁ jitvā rājñaḥ sudurmadān||29||

chakre — took (as his own); danuja-rajasya — of the king of the Danavas; vamane — as Vamana; bhuvana-shriyam — the sovereignty of the worlds; jigye — conquered; tu — and; bhargavah — Bhargava (Parashurama); kshaunim — the earth; jitva — defeating; rajnah — the kings; su-durmadan — arrogant.

29as Vamana He took for Himself the sovereignty of the worlds from the king of the Danavas; and Bhargava8 conquered the earth, defeating the arrogant kings,

Verse 30

ददौ गां ब्राह्मणायैव विष्णुर्लोकैकतारणः।
श्रीरामे रावणं हत्वा यशसापूरितं जगत्॥३०॥

dadau gāṁ brāhmaṇāyaiva viṣṇurlokaikatāraṇaḥ|
śrīrāme rāvaṇaṁ hatvā yaśasāpūritaṁ jagat||30||

dadau — gave; gam — the earth; brahmanaya — to a brahmana; eva — indeed; vishnuh — Vishnu; loka-eka-taranah — the sole deliverer of the world; shri-rame — as Sri Rama; ravanam — Ravana; hatva — having slain; yashasa — with glory; apuritam — was filled; jagat — the world.

30and Vishnu, the sole deliverer of the world, gave that earth to a brahmana. As Sri Rama He slew Ravana, and the world was filled with His glory.

Verse 31

श्रीमत्कृष्णावतारे तु भूमेर्भारावतारणम्।
स्वयमेव हरिस्तत्र सर्वशक्तिसमन्वितः॥३१॥

śrīmatkṛṣṇāvatāre tu bhūmerbhārāvatāraṇam|
svayameva haristatra sarvaśaktisamanvitaḥ||31||

shrimat-krishna-avatare — in the descent of Sriman Krishna; tu — and; bhumeh — of the earth; bhara-avataranam — the removal of the burden; svayam eva — himself; harih — Hari; tatra — there; sarva-shakti-samanvitah — endowed with all powers.

31And in the descent of Sriman Krishna, Hari Himself, endowed with all powers, removed the burden of the earth.

Verse 32

बौद्धे तु मोहनं चक्रे वेदानां भगवान्परः।
म्लेच्छानां निधनं चैव कल्किरूपेण सोऽकरोत्॥३२॥

bauddhe tu mohanaṁ cakre vedānāṁ bhagavānparaḥ|
mlecchānāṁ nidhanaṁ caiva kalkirūpeṇa so'karot||32||

bauddhe — as the Buddha; tu — and; mohanam — bewilderment; chakre — produced; vedanam — regarding the Vedas; bhagavan — Bhagavan; parah — the Supreme; mlechchhanam — of the mlechchhas; nidhanam — destruction; cha eva — and also; kalki-rupena — in the form of Kalki; sah — he; akarot — accomplished.

32As the Buddha the Supreme Bhagavan bewildered (people) regarding the Vedas, and in the form of Kalki He destroyed the mlechchhas.

Verse 33

एवंविधान्यनेकानि कर्माणि बहुरूपिणः।
कार्यावतारा नृहरेः कथिताः परमर्षिभिः॥३३॥

evaṁvidhānyanekāni karmāṇi bahurūpiṇaḥ|
kāryāvatārā nṛhareḥ kathitāḥ paramarṣibhiḥ||33||

evam-vidhani — of this kind; anekani — many; karmani — deeds; bahu-rupinah — of the many-formed; karya-avatarah — the avataras for a task; nrihareh — of Nrihari; kathitah — are described; parama-rshibhih — by the great rishis.

33Such are the many deeds of the many-formed Nrihari; these avataras who descend for a particular task have been described by the great rishis."

Thus ends the fourth sarga, "On the Descents" (Avatara-anukarana), of the first prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Nrihari ("Man-Hari") is usually a name of Nrisimha; here, as in v. 33, it names the Lord in general.
  2. The sense is that a single portion of the Lord appeared in two ways — as Madhavendra Puri and as Advaita Acharya. "Portion" does not diminish Advaita: in Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching He is Maha-Vishnu Himself (together with Sadashiva), non-different from the Lord; Madhavendra Puri is His guru and the root of the tree of devotion.
  3. The brahmana's account itself is not given in the poem; Murari relates only its substance (vv. 9–11). Possibly "Bitten by a Snake" (Nagadashta) is the brahmana's name.
  4. According to tradition, Haridasa is a portion of Brahma, who appeared as a devotee to atone for an offence.
  5. "Portion" (amsha) does not diminish Nityananda here: in the same verse Murari calls Him "the Lord Himself," and in v. 15 "the second form of Sri Krishna." According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Nityananda is Balarama Himself.
  6. The avatara of the Dvapara age is usually named otherwise; here Murari Gupta names Prithu, the king who first established the order of worship. The Bhagavata Purana (11.5.27–28) describes the avatara of the Dvapara age differently: dark-complexioned, in yellow garments, bearing the marks of Vishnu, worshipped according to the rules of the Vedas and tantras.
  7. Sri Chaitanya is the yuga-avatara of the Kali age, who establishes sankirtana (cf. Bhagavata Purana 11.5.32); yet He is not one avatara among others: in Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching He is Krishna Himself, Svayam Bhagavan, in the mood and lustre of Radha (so Murari too, 4.20.19 and 4.26.18).
  8. Bhargava is Parashurama, the descendant of Bhrigu.
